title: Possibilities of Utilising Biomass Collected from Road Verges to Produce Biogas and Biodiesel
authors: Robert Czubaszek; Agnieszka Wysocka-Czubaszek; Aneta Sienkiewicz; Alicja Piotrowska-Niczyporuk; Martin J. Wassen; Andrzej Bajguz
source_location: Table 1, p. 4 (seasonal chemistry); Table 8, p. 12 (summed FAMEs)
geography: Białystok, Podlaskie Voivodeship, Poland (53°07′ N, 23°09′ E)
material_scope: Street-side mowing piles dominated by Lolium perenne, with Poa pratensis and Festuca rubra; samples collected 25 April, 31 July and 7 October 2019; fresh grass and material ensiled 5–6 weeks
sample_design: Three replicates per season and material state; report values are mean ± standard deviation
methods: Fresh-grass moisture determined by drying at 105 ± 2 °C to constant mass; volatile solids, TKN, total P, K, Na and TOC reported on dry-matter basis. FAMEs were quantified by GC-MS/SIM after hexane extraction and methanol-KOH transesterification.

source_tables.fields: Total solids, volatile solids, pH, TKN, total phosphorus, potassium, sodium, total organic carbon
Summed MUFA, PUFA, SFA and total FAME measurements

unit_and_basis_notes: Table 1 composition measurements are reported on the table-specific basis recorded in each CSV row. Table 8 FAME sums are µg/g dry matter. FAME concentration is not equivalent to crude fat, ether extract, total lipid, or a directly transferable GreenHub Lipids mass fraction.
uncertainty_note: Study reports standard deviations for n=3; between-site, interannual, species-mix, sampling, and method-transfer uncertainty for GreenHub are not quantified.
limitations: Polish roadside material is a literature comparator, not the GreenHub/VARTA sample and not a Dutch default.
Season and preservation state materially affect composition; the six conditions must not be averaged into one assumed GreenHub feed profile.
FAME sums cannot replace the model's crude-lipid/ether-extract component because the analytes and methods differ.
Total TKN, P, K, and Na do not establish ammonium, organic/particulate N, or dissolved/particulate nutrient speciation.
Reference observations are not activated as UI inputs or process defaults.
